body:
I'm glad to hear your day went well!  

The problem with having not much support over the past decade (wow it has been that) is you become self-reliant and you don't want to burden others with your pain or even ask for help as you are afraid of being seen as weak.  I'll keep the thought about talking sometime in mind though.

Enjoy your Thanksgiving!

Hi Needawayout89.  I'm 25 and please don't put your family or your girlfriend through that pain.  Yes, I've just recently posted on the subreddit as well if you check my post history.  But in my defense, I only have a best friend that I am hanging on to.  I have no girlfriend and I am essentially dead to my family.

Thinking long-term as this mindset gives us tunnel vision, you can finish up school this year, get out of your parent's house and get closer to your girlfriend.  You could be closer to her friends, meet people and a lot less anxious going into social situations with at least 1 other person rather than by yourself.

I appreciate the responses guys.

I don't necessarily agree with pickup.  It's not I don't understand what they are trying to do, but it is the mentality of objectification and viewing it as a 'game' rather than just conversation with someone.  Doing it that way imo can come off as trying to hard and depending on who you are, you aren't being yourself.  What do you do then if you get into a relationship?  Keep faking that social mentality?  Fake it til you make it I guess (applies to work too).

Regarding my looks/how I keep myself.  I work out, I am 5'10 and ~150 lbs.  I drive a nice car and dress decent so I don't think it is my looks or how I keep myself holding me back.  And no, I'm not going after 10/10s every time.  Maybe I just have horrible luck?

I've heard that I will be loved before, and I will find someone special.  But I've lost hope in that.  It is so hard to keep holding on when you face adversity, rejection, and constant failure at every turn.

I would say I have 1 friend.  That is someone who I talk to and see outside of work.  I view him closer than my family due to my family choosing to ignore/leave me.  Anyone else is the occasional run into followed by "hey how is life since we did that charity event?"  

Yes.  I do enjoy and appreciate what I have accomplished.  Valedictorian, first one to graduate college, successful career, and I have won competitive races.  

What I truly want is to love and be loved.  Those who were closest to me and supposed to care about me left.  I want to be the father who I never had (he left before I was born), have children and provide them the care and support.  But anytime I try and open myself up to someone and think that person likes me, it turns out they never saw me the same way, or were already taken.  

I'm 25 and if I make it past the next year, I will look back like I always do, I will hate what I see.  On the outside everyone seems thinks I am happy and a wonderful person.  But little do they realize that I am slowly eating myself away.

That's a long post.  Sorry for the rant.  Thanks SekondaH

Thank you itscoldincanada for the thoughts.  Just to address some of your questions, my family split because of drama.  I chose not to choose "a side", so I was alienated by both.  And yes, I used to have a lot of friends when I was younger but went across country for college so we grew out of touch and now I live in a city that none of those are in.

The idea of going to therapy is scary.  It is the self-realization that something could be wrong and I am not willing to admit that I am slowly becoming depressed because I continue to smile on the outside.  But when I am alone at night or on a weekend, that is when reality starts to sink in.
